questions.q: At midspan of a singly reinforced simple beam, the main bars sit:
questions.n: Positive moment puts the bottom in tension.

questions.q: Uniform live load for residential occupancy in the NSCP:
questions.n: Basic floor areas in dwellings take 1.9 kPa.

questions.q: End-bearing piles are typically chosen for:
o: Saving money compared with shallow footings
Situations where friction carries the load
Large, tall buildings over deep firm strata
questions.n: They transfer heavy loads to rock or hard layers.

questions.q: The floor area whose load a member carries is its:
questions.n: Also called the influence area.

questions.q: The thick concrete block that ties a group of piles to the column is the:
questions.n: The pile cap spreads column load to the piles.

questions.q: Thin concrete shells became rare in North America after the 1960s mainly because:
questions.n: Curved formwork is labor-intensive.

questions.q: A five-storey addition on coarse-grained (sand and gravel) soil will most likely sit on:
o: A thick mat over the whole site
questions.n: Granular soils usually have good bearing near the surface.

questions.q: Which structural element works in pure tension?
questions.n: Cables can only pull; arches work in compression.

questions.q: Which form develops hoop forces in its rings?
questions.n: Domes carry meridional and hoop (circumferential) forces.

questions.q: Minimum cover for primary bars in plant-cast precast beams and columns not exposed to weather:
o: db, but at least 15 mm and need not exceed 40 mm
questions.n: Plant control allows reduced cover.

questions.q: A pad footing under a single column is an:
questions.n: One column, one pad.

questions.q: Which statement about bundled bars is WRONG?
o: Bundles must be enclosed by ties or stirrups
A bundle may hold no more than three bars
Bars over 36 mm can't be bundled in beams
Cut-offs in a bundle must stagger at least 40 db
questions.n: Up to four bars may be bundled.

questions.q: Lateral loads such as wind and earthquake act:
questions.n: Lateral means horizontal.

questions.q: Along a seismic beam, outside the zones that need hoops, stirrups are spaced at most:
questions.n: Hoops are required near the ends; d/2 elsewhere.

questions.q: The Philippines has two seismic zones in the NSCP. Which province lies mostly in the lower-hazard Zone 2?
questions.n: Palawan (with Sulu and Tawi-Tawi) is Zone 2; the rest of the country is Zone 4.

questions.q: Extra bars placed around a slab opening to pick up the interrupted reinforcement are:
questions.n: Trimmers frame the opening.

questions.q: A space frame is strong for its weight mainly because of:
o: The rigidity of its triangulated geometry
questions.n: Triangles don't change shape under load.

questions.q: A 3.3 m RC column needs lap splices in its vertical bars. Where should they go?
o: In the middle half of the height, about 0.825 m to 2.475 m up
questions.n: Laps are kept out of the high-moment zones at the ends; the middle half avoids them.

questions.q: Long members driven deep to carry loads down to firm strata form a:
questions.n: Piles bypass weak surface soil.

questions.q: A two-way slab carried directly on columns with no beams is a:
questions.n: Flat slabs, often with drop panels, sit directly on columns.

questions.q: Punching shear in a slab is mainly caused by:
o: A concentrated load, such as a column
questions.n: Heavy point loads punch through around columns or footings.

questions.q: In prestressed precast work, the jacking force is applied to the:
questions.n: Jacks tension the strands before or after casting.

questions.q: Typical concrete cover to the main bars of beams and columns not exposed to earth:
questions.n: 40 mm protects bars in beams and columns; 75 mm is for concrete cast against earth.

questions.q: Laminated seismic base isolators are built mainly of:
questions.n: Rubber bearings decouple the building from ground motion.

questions.q: In a continuous RC beam, top bars are lapped:
o: Near midspan, where top tension is low
questions.n: Top bars are in tension over supports, so splices go where tension is low, near midspan.

questions.q: The beam spanning over a door or window opening is a:
questions.n: Lintels carry the wall above openings.

questions.q: A short, stocky column normally fails by:
questions.n: Buckling governs slender columns, not short ones.

questions.q: A wall built to hold back earth is a:
questions.n: Retaining walls resist lateral soil pressure.
